goldens.comment: The findMembers() call is now asynchronous and unhandled. The controller may not have member data immediately available, creating a race condition.

In the next action, capping the next offset at user_count can produce an empty page (e.g., total equal to limit results in offset == total, showing 2/2 with no members). This can cause confusing UX on the last page.
The remove_member test uses xhr :put to call the remove_member action, but the route defines delete 'members' => 'groups#remove_member' requiring DELETE method.

The `totalPages` calculation using `Math.floor(user_count / limit) + 1` produces an extra page when `user_count` is an exact multiple of `limit`, leading to incorrect pagination. For example, with 100 users and a limit of 50, it reports 3 pages instead of 2, allowing navigation to an empty page.
Expected to return a value at the end of function - code paths without explicit returns will return undefined

The route provides the group's ID in params[:id], but the code attempts to read it from params[:group_id], causing the action to fail. This results in a broken feature when trying to access group memberships.

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/assets/javascripts/admin/controllers/admin-group.js.es6:62 — Unresolved `TODO` admits the add-members input is not cleared after submission.

adjudication.rationale: The finding points to line 62 in admin-group.js.es6 where there is a TODO comment: '// TODO: should clear the input'. This is indeed present in the diff in the addMembers action. However, a TODO comment is not a bug or defect - it's a note about a potential future improvement. The code functions correctly (it adds members when usernames are provided), it just doesn't clear the input field afterward. This is a minor UX issue at most, not a correctness problem, security issue, or bug. The finding is essentially flagging a TODO comment as a problem, which is more of a style/documentation observation than a real defect.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [lens/architecture][lens/intent-preservation] app/controllers/groups_controller.rb:22 — The public members endpoint now returns only 50 members, while `group-members.js.es6:11` performs one fetch with no paging controls; larger groups silently appear incomplete.

adjudication.rationale: Looking at the diff for app/assets/javascripts/discourse/routes/group-members.js.es6, the setupController now calls model.findMembers() which sets up pagination with limit/offset. The findMembers() method in group.js sets limit: 50 and offset: 0 as defaults. However, examining the group/members.hbs template, it iterates over 'members' which is set by findMembers(). The issue is that the public group members page (not admin) doesn't have pagination controls added in this diff - the template just shows {{#each m in members}} without any next/previous buttons. The admin group page (admin/templates/group.hbs) does have pagination controls added. So for the public-facing group members page, users will only see the first 50 members with no way to see more. This is a real functional limitation introduced by this change.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [lens/architecture] app/assets/javascripts/admin/controllers/admin-group.js.es6:13 — `Math.floor(user_count / limit) + 1` creates an empty extra page whenever the count is an exact multiple of the page size.
matched_golden_ids: In the next action, capping the next offset at user_count can produce an empty page (e.g., total equal to limit results in offset == total, showing 2/2 with no members). This can cause confusing UX on the last page.

The `totalPages` calculation using `Math.floor(user_count / limit) + 1` produces an extra page when `user_count` is an exact multiple of `limit`, leading to incorrect pagination. For example, with 100 users and a limit of 50, it reports 3 pages instead of 2, allowing navigation to an empty page.
adjudication_records.primary_judge_reasoning: Both comments identify the same underlying issue: the pagination logic creates an empty page when the count is an exact multiple of the page size. The golden comment describes this from the perspective of the 'next' action capping offset at user_count, while the candidate describes it from the perspective of the page count calculation. Both are pointing to the same confusing UX problem where users see an empty last page when total equals limit or is an exact multiple.

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/controllers/groups_controller.rb:22 — The client-supplied `limit` has no upper or positive bound, allowing arbitrarily large membership queries and invalid zero/negative pagination.

adjudication.rationale: Looking at the diff in app/controllers/groups_controller.rb, line 22 shows `limit = (params[:limit] || 50).to_i`. This takes a client-supplied limit parameter and converts it to an integer with no upper bound validation. A malicious client could pass limit=1000000 to retrieve all users in one query, causing performance issues. Additionally, there's no validation for positive values - a zero or negative limit could cause unexpected behavior. The offset also has no validation (`offset = params[:offset].to_i`). This is a real security/performance issue where user input is not properly validated.

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/controllers/groups_controller.rb:28 — The existing members API response changes from an array to `{members, meta}` without versioning or compatibility handling, breaking unchanged consumers.

adjudication.rationale: The diff clearly shows the members endpoint in groups_controller.rb changing from `render_serialized(members.to_a, GroupUserSerializer)` (which returns an array) to `render json: { members: serialize_data(...), meta: { total, limit, offset } }` (which returns an object with members and meta keys). This is a breaking API change - any existing client code expecting an array response will break when it receives an object instead. The finding correctly identifies this as a compatibility issue.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [lens/intent-preservation] app/controllers/admin/groups_controller.rb:34 — Existing PATCH and nested PUT membership contracts are silently ignored; missing flat `visible` also becomes `false`, so legacy requests can report success while hiding the group and making no membership change.

adjudication.rationale: Looking at the diff, the old controller had separate `update_patch` and `update_put` methods that handled PATCH requests differently (for incremental add/delete of members via `params[:changes]`) and PUT requests (which handled `params[:group][:usernames]` for bulk membership). The new `update` method only handles flat parameters like `params[:alias_level]`, `params[:visible]`, and `params[:name]` - it completely removes support for both the PATCH incremental changes and the nested `params[:group][:usernames]` format. If legacy clients send requests in the old format (e.g., `{group: {visible: 'true', usernames: '...'}}` or PATCH with `{changes: {add: '...'}}`), the new controller will silently ignore those parameters and return success. The `visible` parameter now expects `params[:visible]` directly, not `params[:group][:visible]`, so legacy requests would have `visible` default to false (since `params[:visible]` would be nil). This is a real backward compatibility issue where the API contract changed silently.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [lens/architecture] app/assets/javascripts/discourse/models/group.js:30 — Concurrent `findMembers()` requests write to the same pagination/member state without cancellation or generation checks, allowing an older response to overwrite the latest page or mutation refresh.

adjudication.rationale: Looking at the diff, the findMembers() function in group.js makes an AJAX request and then calls setProperties to update user_count, limit, offset, and members on the model. The code shows that pagination actions (next/previous) call findMembers(), and addMembers/removeMember also call findMembers() after their operations complete. There is no cancellation mechanism or request tracking visible in the diff. If a user rapidly clicks pagination buttons or if a member removal triggers findMembers() while another request is in flight, the responses could arrive out of order and the older response could overwrite the newer state. This is a real race condition - the code sets state directly from async responses without any guards against stale data.
